title: Count Geonor Boss Guide: Phases, Dangerous Attacks and Preparation
summary: Complete Act 1 boss guide covering the humanoid phase and the wolf phase (the mist sub-phase is part of the wolf transformation), with an attack table, community solutions, and class strategy.

sections.title: Remember These Three Things First
sections.callout: Do not chase adds during the fog phase.
calloutDetail: Keep your character in a position where you can observe the boss dash direction. Prioritise lateral movement space over killing distant wolves.
Only clear minions that block your movement path or continuously interrupt your actions.

answers.label: Before the fight
answers.text: Put cold resistance, movement speed and recovery on the same checklist. Do not only look at DPS.

answers.label: During the fight
answers.text: Move first after seeing a telegraph, then find an output window. Stop attacking during phase transitions.

answers.label: After repeated deaths
answers.text: Identify which specific attack killed you, then go to the matching troubleshooting entry instead of blindly swapping gear.

items.label: Cold resistance and effective life
checks: Multiple phases apply cold pressure and melee hits simultaneously.
items.why: Frost attacks in human and wolf phases deal significant cold damage on top of physical hits.
items.fix: Temporarily swap rings, amulet or resistance affixes. Even a 10% improvement reduces consecutive-hit deaths.

items.label: Boot movement speed
checks: Determines whether you can leave an attack line before the telegraph completes.
items.why: The fog dash and wolf leap have short wind-ups that punish slow characters.
items.fix: Prioritise boots with movement speed. You do not need rarity — a magic pair with 20% speed helps immediately.

items.label: Single-target damage rotation
checks: The longer the fight lasts, the lower your margin in the fog phase.
items.why: Extended fights mean more fog-phase repetitions and more chances to be caught.
items.fix: Separate your mapping and boss skill setups. Verify that support gems actually match your main skill tags.

items.label: Recovery and resources
checks: Phase transitions drain resources while you cannot deal damage.
items.why: Players often use all flask charges during the human phase, leaving none for the high-pressure wolf phase.
items.fix: Save at least two flask charges for the wolf phase. Remove high-cost supports that contribute little single-target damage.

items.label: Mobility and crowd control
checks: Being slowed then rolling may already miss the safe window.
items.why: Cold damage applies chill and freeze, reducing your ability to reposition.
items.fix: Confirm your dash skill is available. Understand that dodge roll cannot escape persistent ground effects.

phases.label: Phase 1: Humanoid
objectives: Learn the weapon swing tell and the ground-rune pattern.
Stay to the side-rear and watch for the end of his attacks.
Save recovery resources for later phases.
notes: The humanoid phase is the best time to learn the boss's rhythm. Don't use long combos—wait for the swing to finish, then land a full single-target rotation.
Frost runes appear under your feet. Step out first, then decide whether you can return to deal damage.

phases.label: Phase 2: Wolf (includes the mist sub-phase)
phases.trigger: At ~50% health he transforms; the health pool resets to full and the wolf phase begins.
objectives: During the mist sub-phase, focus on lateral movement to dodge the repeated charges—don't greed damage.
Wait for the full combo to end before your burst rotation.
Keep your dash available to reposition after the leap landing.
notes: Before the wolf phase properly starts there is a mist sub-phase: Count Geonor is invulnerable in the fog and dashes at you 6 times. You cannot damage him during this window—prioritize lateral movement to dodge the charges; once the fog clears the wolf fight begins.
The wolf phase attacks are more continuous. One move ending does not mean you are safe—wait for the full combo to finish.
On transformation the health pool resets to full (full reset), so save recovery resources for this final phase rather than burning them early.
Chilling Breath also appears in the wolf phase and applies freeze, making later attacks harder to dodge.

sections.title: Attack Reference: Telegraphs, Responses and Common Failures

attacks.name: Frost Throw
telegraph: Raises weapon high with a brief pause. A frost glow appears on the blade.
responses: Move to the side-rear to avoid the linear impact zone.
commonMistakes: Backing into the arena wall, leaving no escape for the next attack.

attacks.name: Armoured Charge
telegraph: Body lowers and aims toward the player with a charging pose.
responses: Move laterally or dodge-roll after the lock-in completes.
commonMistakes: Rolling too early — the boss re-aims before the dash fires.
notes: Wait for the lock-in animation to finish before committing your dodge.

attacks.name: Fog Dash
telegraph: A voice line plays just before the boss emerges from the fog.
responses: Maintain lateral movement. Leave room for a second direction change.
commonMistakes: Stopping to cast while clearing minions, becoming a stationary target.
notes: The voice cue is the most reliable indicator. Stop long animations the moment you hear it.

attacks.name: Summon Wolves
telegraph: Multiple targets appear at the arena edges.
responses: Only clear wolves blocking your movement route. Keep watching the boss.
commonMistakes: Chasing distant wolves and losing boss visibility.
notes: Wolves that do not block your path are not worth the repositioning cost.

attacks.name: Wolf Leap Strike
telegraph: Head raises, body pulls back, then locks onto a landing spot.
responses: Wait for the landing marker to appear, then leave the marked area.
commonMistakes: Chain-rolling on head-raise, exhausting all movement space before the actual landing.
notes: Patience is key. One well-timed move beats three panic rolls.

attacks.name: Chilling Frost Breath
telegraph: The boss inhales visibly and frost particles gather at the mouth.
responses: Dodge-roll to the side. The breath covers a frontal cone.
commonMistakes: Standing still because the cone looks narrow — it is wider than it appears.
notes: Applies chill on hit, making subsequent attacks harder to dodge.

sections.title: Build-Specific Strategy
paragraphs: Melee: Do not treat 'staying glued to the boss' as the goal. In the human phase, practise entering after his swing ends. In the fog phase, prioritise survival and boss visibility. In the wolf phase, only commit a full rotation after a complete combo ends.

Ranged: The most common ranged failure is retreating to the arena wall. Maintain mid-distance lateral movement. Use short-cast skills to add damage between boss attacks rather than continuous backpedalling.

Minion: You still need to actively observe the boss. Do not stand still because your minions are dealing damage. In the fog phase, keep your character moving and confirm your minions have not dragged the fight to the visibility edge.

Low movement speed: Stay near the arena centre. Pre-position before attacks land. Use only the shortest animation skills. Do not wait for the danger zone to fully appear before moving — react to the telegraph start.
bullets: If damage feels too low, verify your skill-setup, weapon base damage and support compatibility before upgrading gear.
If survival feels impossible, separate resistance, effective life and movement space into three independent checks.

entries.question: Why do I keep dying in the fog phase even with cold resistance?
summary: A player describes stopping to clear wolves during the fog, then being hit by the boss dash and ground effects in quick succession.
editorialAnalysis: This is not purely a cold resistance problem. Visibility, stationary time and movement route all fail simultaneously when players prioritise add-clear over positioning.
officialAnswer: Maintain lateral movement first. Only clear wolves that block your path. After identifying the actual killing attack, check the corresponding defence in the troubleshooting section.

entries.question: Does melee simply have no output time in the fog phase?
summary: Some players choose to wait out the phase entirely. Others only use a single quick skill after each dash ends.
editorialAnalysis: Both approaches can work. The difference comes from attack speed, character recovery animation and familiarity with the dash rhythm.
officialAnswer: For a first kill, prioritise survival. Once familiar with the rhythm, use one quick-recovery skill after the dash ends. Do not force a full combo.

entries.question: Do I need to kill all the summoned wolves first?
summary: Community comments frequently disagree on whether to clear the arena or focus the boss.
editorialAnalysis: The page should give a conditional answer based on whether wolves block movement or cause continuous interrupts, rather than a fixed 'clear all' instruction.
officialAnswer: Only clear wolves that enter your movement route or continuously stagger you. Wolves far from your path are not worth losing boss visibility.

problems.symptom: Why am I still being one-shot despite decent cold resistance?
directAnswer: The killing blow likely includes physical damage, consecutive hits, or a high-damage attack that requires active avoidance. Capped resistance does not mean you can stand still.
checks: Confirm whether death occurred in the human, fog or wolf phase.
Cross-reference the attack table to identify whether it was the dash, leap or ground overlap.
Check effective life, armour/evasion and recovery — not just cold resistance.

problems.symptom: When can melee attack during the fog phase?
directAnswer: For a first kill, focus on movement. Once familiar with the rhythm, use one quick-recovery skill after the boss dash ends and your route is clear.
checks: Do not attempt full long combos.
If wolves block your retreat, clear the nearest one first.
Stop attacking immediately when the next voice cue begins.

problems.symptom: Is my damage too low — do I need better gear first?
directAnswer: Not necessarily. First confirm you are using a single-target skill setup, that supports actually match your skill tags, and that your weapon base damage is not behind for the current act.
checks: Compare weapon base damage against attack/cast speed.
Verify support gems are compatible with your main skill tags.
Separate mapping tools from boss tools — do not sacrifice all single-target for area.

problems.symptom: Do I need to clear all summoned wolves before attacking the boss?
directAnswer: Only clear wolves that block your movement route, cause continuous stagger, or prevent you from observing the boss.
checks: Chasing wolves at the arena edge usually costs you more important boss telegraph information.
If wolves are far from your path, ignore them and focus on positioning.
